items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I got indoctrination into John Cage and Roger Sessions and you know Stockhausen.

ctx.x: If you’re doing that kind of thing do you feel compelled to sort of then bring it back to something that sounds less out? You know what I mean by that? I mean some people would play sort of outside the change or add all those things on and then they would sort of bring it back as if I went out there but I’m going to bring you back.

No I don’t think so. I think, you know, in other words, that’s the thing, in other words the more that you can make it sound like it’s not out or in or whatever, the more that you can make it sound like it’s a part of it, then you’re doing your job. Because sometimes what happens, somebody’ll play something and it’s obvious that they’re playing it — I mean like think about a lot of the things that Charlie Parker played, I mean he would play a lot of things where, you know, he would play like a half-step above and…
Well what’s it like to try to make a living in music these days?
